about: Odile's gender shows only in a 'She' two sentences after her name, which the pronoun reader (same or next sentence) cannot see; Bram's shows only by his/him, which the reader counts when no subject pronoun contradicts it.
title: The Pear Ferry
author: Lina Marsh

chapters.title: One
paragraphs: The ferry left the harbour at dawn, and the mist lay low over the water. Odile stood at the rail with a basket of pears. The gulls followed the wake for a mile. She counted the boats that passed the lighthouse.
Bram carried the ropes to the stern on his shoulder. The deck was wet and the planks were slick. The captain shouted a warning across the deck.
The captain paid Bram at noon and thanked him for the work. A bell rang somewhere below the deck. The engine coughed twice and then ran smoothly.
Odile sat on a coil of rope near the bow. The wind was cold for the season. She pulled a scarf from the basket and wrapped it twice.
Nobody spoke for a long while. The town on the far shore grew slowly from a smudge into roofs and chimneys. Smoke rose from a dozen kitchens.
Bram tied the last knot and wiped his hands on a rag. The ferry turned towards the pier. The pilot leaned on the wheel and squinted.
Odile looked at the roofs and the chimneys. The pears smelled of late summer. She thought of the orchard behind the mill.
The pier was crowded with carts and barrels. A dog barked at the gulls. The ropes were thrown and caught.

chapters.title: Two
paragraphs: The market opened at eight, and the stalls filled the square. Odile set the basket on a barrel by the fountain. A boy ran past with a hoop and a stick. She sold the first pears before the church bell had finished.
Bram came up from the pier with a sack on his back. The baker waved from the doorway. The sack was full of flour for the mill.
A carter asked Bram for a hand with a wheel, and the two of them lifted it together. The axle groaned. The carter gave him a coin and a nod.
Odile counted the coins twice. The fountain splashed over the stones. She smiled at the total and tied the purse.
By noon the square was half empty. The stall keepers ate bread and cheese in the shade. Pigeons picked at the crumbs.
Bram walked over to the fountain and tipped his cap.
The two of them shared the last pear. The bell rang for the afternoon. The ferry would leave again at four.
